```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

# Paths relative to this Rmd's location (Adriana_analysis/scripts/)
project_dir <- ".."
load(file.path(project_dir, "project_functions.rda"))

paths       <- setup_project_paths(project_dir)
tables_dir  <- paths$tables_dir
figures_dir <- paths$figures_dir
output_dir  <- paths$output_dir
```

```{r libraries}
library(tidyverse)
library(broom)

select <- dplyr::select

# Shared colour palette for dissertation figures
load(file.path(project_dir, "project_colours.rda"))
```

```{r config}
# Single switch for which TPM column to regress against cell volume.
# TPMsc = spike-in-normalised TPM (S. cerevisiae fraction), matching
# the project's established S. pombe spike-in normalisation approach
# used throughout the rest of the pipeline. Log2-transformed here with
# a +1 pseudocount (TPMsc has ~0.8% zero values, no negatives, so +1
# is a safe minimal offset).
#
# log2TPMnorm4 was considered as an alternative (already log2-
# transformed in df_sc_final) but rejected: comparing the two showed
# they are NOT simply log2(TPMsc + 1) - log2TPMnorm4 is consistently
# lower and appears to be normalised against a different reference
# (likely TPMmean4/TPMmin4, based on column naming), i.e. a variant
# built for a different purpose elsewhere in the pipeline rather than
# a general-purpose expression value. TPMsc matches the project's
# standard normalisation used throughout.
#
# To switch to log2TPMnorm4 instead: set tpm_col <- "log2TPMnorm4" and
# set log_transform <- FALSE below (it's already logged).
tpm_col        <- "TPMsc"
log_transform   <- TRUE
log_pseudocount <- 1
```

```{r load-data}
# df_sc_final.txt: long format, one row per gene x sample (5,190 genes
# x 93 samples = 482,670 rows). mean_cell_volume is already present per
# sample - no join to PCA_samples_AC.txt needed.
df_sc_final <- read_tsv(file.path(tables_dir, "df_sc_final.txt"),
                        show_col_types = FALSE)

cat("df_sc_final:", nrow(df_sc_final), "rows |",
    n_distinct(df_sc_final$gene_id), "genes |",
    n_distinct(df_sc_final$sample), "samples\n")

cat("Using TPM column:", tpm_col,
    "| log-transforming:", log_transform, "\n")
```

```{r prepare-expression-data}
# Build the gene x sample expression + volume table. Drop rows with
# missing TPM or missing cell volume (a per-gene regression needs both
# to be non-NA for a given sample to contribute).
expr_data <- df_sc_final %>%
  dplyr::select(gene_id, gene_name, sample, all_of(tpm_col), mean_cell_volume) %>%
  rename(tpm_value = all_of(tpm_col)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(tpm_value), !is.na(mean_cell_volume))

if (log_transform) {
  expr_data <- expr_data %>%
    mutate(log2_expr = log2(tpm_value + log_pseudocount))
} else {
  expr_data <- expr_data %>%
    mutate(log2_expr = tpm_value)
}

cat("Rows retained after filtering NA:", nrow(expr_data), "\n")
cat("Genes retained:", n_distinct(expr_data$gene_id), "\n")
cat("Samples retained:", n_distinct(expr_data$sample), "\n")

# Sanity check: samples per gene should be consistent (close to 93) -
# large variation would indicate uneven NA dropout across genes
samples_per_gene <- expr_data %>% count(gene_id) %>% pull(n)
cat("\nSamples per gene - min:", min(samples_per_gene),
    "| median:", median(samples_per_gene),
    "| max:", max(samples_per_gene), "\n")
```

```{r per-gene-regression-function}
# For each gene: Spearman correlation (rho, p-value) between log2
# expression and mean cell volume across samples, matching the
# Spearman approach used elsewhere in the pipeline (e.g. PC1/PC2 vs
# cell volume), plus a linear regression slope (log2 expression units
# per unit cell volume) for genes wanting an explicit slope value.
# Minimum 10 samples per gene required for a stable correlation
# estimate (arbitrary but conservative given ~93 samples available for
# most genes).
run_gene_regression <- function(df, min_samples = 10) {
  df %>%
    group_by(gene_id, gene_name) %>%
    filter(n() >= min_samples) %>%
    summarise(
      n_samples = n(),
      spearman_rho     = suppressWarnings(
        cor(log2_expr, mean_cell_volume, method = "spearman")
      ),
      spearman_p       = suppressWarnings(
        cor.test(log2_expr, mean_cell_volume, method = "spearman")$p.value
      ),
      lm_slope         = coef(lm(log2_expr ~ mean_cell_volume))[["mean_cell_volume"]],
      lm_slope_se      = summary(lm(log2_expr ~ mean_cell_volume))$coefficients["mean_cell_volume", "Std. Error"],
      lm_p             = summary(lm(log2_expr ~ mean_cell_volume))$coefficients["mean_cell_volume", "Pr(>|t|)"],
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

cat("Running per-gene regression (this may take a moment for ~5,000 genes)...\n")
gene_volume_reg <- run_gene_regression(expr_data)

cat("Genes with regression results:", nrow(gene_volume_reg), "\n")
```

```{r fdr-correction}
# BH correction across all tested genes, for both the Spearman and the
# linear model p-values, matching the FDR approach used throughout the
# rest of the pipeline (e.g. mitch's p.adjustMANOVA, script 09's
# p.adjust)
gene_volume_reg <- gene_volume_reg %>%
  mutate(
    spearman_padj = p.adjust(spearman_p, method = "BH"),
    lm_padj       = p.adjust(lm_p, method = "BH")
  ) %>%
  arrange(spearman_padj)

n_sig_spearman <- sum(gene_volume_reg$spearman_padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
n_sig_lm       <- sum(gene_volume_reg$lm_padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)

cat("Significant genes (Spearman, FDR < 0.05):", n_sig_spearman,
    "of", nrow(gene_volume_reg), "\n")
cat("Significant genes (linear model, FDR < 0.05):", n_sig_lm,
    "of", nrow(gene_volume_reg), "\n")

cat("\nSpearman rho range:",
    round(min(gene_volume_reg$spearman_rho, na.rm = TRUE), 3), "to",
    round(max(gene_volume_reg$spearman_rho, na.rm = TRUE), 3), "\n")
cat("lm slope range:",
    round(min(gene_volume_reg$lm_slope, na.rm = TRUE), 4), "to",
    round(max(gene_volume_reg$lm_slope, na.rm = TRUE), 4), "\n")
```

```{r check-against-known-tfs}
# Quick validation: check regression results for the TFs already
# identified as PC1/PC2 hits elsewhere in the pipeline (CBF1, IFH1,
# SFP1, ERT1, RTG1, RTG3), as a sense check that this independent
# per-gene metric is broadly consistent with the PCA-based enrichment
# results, not a formal comparison.
#
# NOTE: gene IDs below are from memory of standard S. cerevisiae
# systematic names and have not been independently verified against
# SGD - double check before relying on this chunk's output.
known_tf_ids <- c(
  CBF1 = "YJR060W", IFH1 = "YLR223C", SFP1 = "YLR403W",
  ERT1 = "YBR239C", RTG1 = "YOL067C", RTG3 = "YBL103C"
)

gene_volume_reg %>%
  filter(gene_id %in% known_tf_ids) %>%
  left_join(
    enframe(known_tf_ids, name = "tf_name", value = "gene_id"),
    by = "gene_id"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(tf_name, gene_id, gene_name, n_samples,
         spearman_rho, spearman_padj, lm_slope, lm_padj) %>%
  print(n = Inf)
```

```{r plot-distribution}
# Distribution of per-gene Spearman rho values - sanity check for
# overall shape (expect a spread centred near zero with a meaningful
# tail of both positive and negative correlations, consistent with
# PC2 capturing a real but partial cell-size expression programme).
# Diagnostic only, not a dissertation figure, so its title is left in
# place as a visual aid when reviewing interactively.
p_dist <- ggplot(gene_volume_reg, aes(x = spearman_rho)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60, fill = project_colours[["blue"]],
                 color = "white", alpha = 0.9) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed",
             color = project_colours[["grey"]]) +
  labs(
    title = "Per-gene expression vs cell volume (Spearman rho)",
    subtitle = paste0(
      nrow(gene_volume_reg), " genes | ",
      n_sig_spearman, " significant at FDR < 0.05"
    ),
    x = "Spearman rho (log2 expression vs mean cell volume)",
    y = "Number of genes"
  ) +
  theme_bw()

print(p_dist)
```

```{r load-pc2-loadings}
# Load PC2 gene loadings from the PCA for cross-validation against the
# per-gene Spearman rho above. PC2 was independently established to
# correlate strongly with mean cell volume at the sample level
# (Spearman r = 0.795, PCA_samples_AC.txt) - if per-gene rho tracks
# PC2 loading well, that is independent confirmation (a completely
# different statistical approach - univariate per-gene correlation vs
# multivariate PCA loading) that PC2 genuinely captures cell-size-
# driven expression change, rather than an artefact of the PCA itself.
pca_genes <- read_tsv(file.path(tables_dir, "PCA_genes_AC.txt"),
                      show_col_types = FALSE)

pc2_loadings <- pca_genes %>%
  dplyr::select(gene_id, PC2)

cat("PC2 loadings available for", nrow(pc2_loadings), "genes\n")
```

```{r compare-rho-vs-pc2}
# Join per-gene Spearman rho (expression vs cell volume) with PC2
# loading (from the joint 93-sample PCA) on gene_id, then correlate
# the two. Spearman used again for consistency with the rest of the
# comparison chain, since neither variable is guaranteed to be
# normally distributed.
rho_vs_pc2 <- gene_volume_reg %>%
  inner_join(pc2_loadings, by = "gene_id")

cat("Genes with both a Spearman rho and a PC2 loading:",
    nrow(rho_vs_pc2), "\n")

rho_pc2_cor    <- cor(rho_vs_pc2$spearman_rho, rho_vs_pc2$PC2,
                       method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")
rho_pc2_cortest <- cor.test(rho_vs_pc2$spearman_rho, rho_vs_pc2$PC2,
                             method = "spearman")

cat("\nSpearman correlation between per-gene rho (expr vs volume) and",
    "PC2 loading:\n")
cat("  rho =", round(rho_pc2_cor, 3), "\n")
cat("  p-value =", format(rho_pc2_cortest$p.value, scientific = TRUE, digits = 3), "\n")
```

```{r plot-rho-vs-pc2}
# Scatter of per-gene expression-volume rho against PC2 loading, with
# a loess trend overlay to make the trend visible through the dense
# point cloud. Full-range version (all genes, including the sparse
# |PC2| > 10 tail) - kept for reference/diagnostics. The dissertation
# figure (Figure 10) is the trimmed version below, so no title or
# subtitle is baked in here; the caption lives in the Word document.
p_rho_pc2 <- ggplot(rho_vs_pc2, aes(x = PC2, y = spearman_rho)) +
  geom_point(color = project_colours[["blue"]], alpha = 0.15, size = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", color = "black", se = FALSE,
              linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed",
             color = project_colours[["grey"]]) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed",
             color = project_colours[["grey"]]) +
  labs(
    x = "PC2 gene loading",
    y = "Spearman rho (log2 expression vs mean cell volume)"
  ) +
  theme_bw()

print(p_rho_pc2)
```

```{r identify-pc2-outliers}
# Identify genes with extreme PC2 loadings driving the sparse tail of
# the loess curve in the rho-vs-PC2 plot. Threshold set at |PC2| > 10,
# chosen by inspecting the plot - the dense point cloud sits within
# roughly [-5, 5], so anything beyond -10 is in the sparse region where
# the loess fit is unreliable (few points, wide extrapolation).
pc2_outlier_threshold <- 10

pc2_outliers <- rho_vs_pc2 %>%
  filter(abs(PC2) > pc2_outlier_threshold) %>%
  arrange(PC2) %>%
  dplyr::select(gene_id, gene_name, PC2, spearman_rho, spearman_padj, n_samples)

cat("Genes with |PC2 loading| >", pc2_outlier_threshold, ":",
    nrow(pc2_outliers), "of", nrow(rho_vs_pc2), "total\n\n")

print(pc2_outliers, n = Inf)
```

```{r pc2-outliers-context}
# Quick check: do any of these outlier genes overlap with TFs or gene
# sets already flagged elsewhere in the pipeline (e.g. the CBF1/IFH1/
# SFP1/ERT1/RTG1/RTG3 TF hits, or known ribosomal protein genes), which
# would help explain why their PC2 loading is so extreme rather than
# treating them as unexplained outliers.
if (nrow(pc2_outliers) > 0) {
  cat("Outlier gene IDs for cross-reference against other results:\n")
  print(pc2_outliers$gene_id)

  cat("\nOutlier gene names for cross-reference against other results:\n")
  print(pc2_outliers$gene_name)
} else {
  cat("No genes exceed the |PC2| >", pc2_outlier_threshold, "threshold -",
      "consider lowering the threshold if the loess tail still looks",
      "sparsely supported.\n")
}
```

```{r plot-rho-vs-pc2-trimmed}
# Re-plot restricted to the dense region (|PC2| <= pc2_outlier_threshold)
# for a loess fit that isn't distorted by the sparse tail. This is the
# dissertation figure (Figure 10) - its caption ("n = 4,602 genes, 16
# outliers excluded and listed separately") corresponds to this trimmed
# plot, not the full-range one above. No title or subtitle baked in;
# the caption lives in the Word document, and the outlier count/
# threshold are already reported there rather than in an on-plot
# subtitle.
rho_vs_pc2_trimmed <- rho_vs_pc2 %>%
  filter(abs(PC2) <= pc2_outlier_threshold)

p_rho_pc2_trimmed <- ggplot(rho_vs_pc2_trimmed, aes(x = PC2, y = spearman_rho)) +
  geom_point(color = project_colours[["blue"]], alpha = 0.15, size = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", color = "black", se = FALSE,
              linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed",
             color = project_colours[["grey"]]) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed",
             color = project_colours[["grey"]]) +
  labs(
    x = "PC2 gene loading",
    y = "Spearman rho (log2 expression vs mean cell volume)"
  ) +
  theme_bw()

print(p_rho_pc2_trimmed)
```

```{r save-outputs}
write_tsv(gene_volume_reg,
          file.path(output_dir, "gene_expression_vs_cell_volume.txt"))
write_tsv(rho_vs_pc2,
          file.path(output_dir, "gene_expression_vs_cell_volume_pc2_comparison.txt"))
write_tsv(pc2_outliers,
          file.path(output_dir, "gene_expression_vs_cell_volume_pc2_outliers.txt"))

ggsave(file.path(figures_dir, "gene_expression_vs_cell_volume_dist.png"),
       plot = p_dist, width = 8, height = 6)
ggsave(file.path(figures_dir, "gene_expression_vs_cell_volume_vs_pc2.png"),
       plot = p_rho_pc2, width = 9, height = 7)
ggsave(file.path(figures_dir, "gene_expression_vs_cell_volume_vs_pc2_trimmed.png"),
       plot = p_rho_pc2_trimmed, width = 9, height = 7)

cat("Done - results saved to output_tables/ and figures/\n")
```
